chapters.intro: The everyday words for using a computer, the internet and your DigiD to arrange things online in the Netherlands. Tap 🔊 to hear each Dutch word or phrase spoken.

sections.title: Why this matters
sections.body: In the Netherlands almost everything official is arranged online: an appointment at the gemeente, your taxes, your health insurance. You log in to these sites with your DigiD, so the words on this page come up again and again.

sections.title: De computer & het internet
sections.note: The core words. Notice de or het in front of each noun.

sections.title: What is DigiD?
sections.body: DigiD is your personal digital ID to log in to Dutch government and healthcare websites. You apply for it once with your BSN, then you use the same username and password (and often a code in the DigiD app) every time you arrange something official online. Keep these details safe and never share them by email.

sections.title: DigiD & online regelen
sections.note: Use these when you arrange official things on the internet.

items.en: your personal digital ID for government and healthcare sites
MijnOverheid (your online government inbox and overview)

sections.title: A safe password
sections.body: Choose a wachtwoord that is long and hard to guess, and use a different one for each account. If a site asks for a code from the DigiD app, open the app on your phone and type the code over. The gemeente or the Belastingdienst will never ask for your password by phone or email.

sections.title: Problemen met inloggen
sections.note: Handy when something does not work online.

items.nl: Het lukt niet om in te loggen.
items.en: I am not managing to log in.

items.nl: Kunt u mij helpen met de computer?
items.en: Can you help me with the computer?
Where do I have to click?

sections.q: U wilt online een afspraak maken bij de gemeente. De website vraagt eerst om uw DigiD. Wat doet u?
sections.qEn: You want to make an appointment with the municipality online. The website first asks for your DigiD. What do you do?
options: Ik stuur mijn wachtwoord in een e-mail.
sections.explanation: Government websites use DigiD to check who you are, so you log in with DigiD. You never send your password by email, and 112 is only for real emergencies.

chapters.intro: The words and phrases you need to rent a home in the Netherlands, sign a contract and sort out problems with your landlord. Tap 🔊 to hear each Dutch word or phrase spoken.

sections.title: Renting in the Netherlands
sections.body: Most newcomers rent through a woningcorporatie (social housing) or via a makelaar on the private market. You sign a huurcontract, pay a borg up front and then pay the huur every month. If your income is low, you may get huurtoeslag (rent benefit) from the Belastingdienst.

sections.title: Huren & het contract
sections.note: The core renting words. Notice de or het in front of each noun.

sections.title: Borg & service charges
sections.body: The borg (also called de waarborgsom) is a deposit you pay before you move in; you get it back when you leave if the home is clean and undamaged. The servicekosten are extra monthly costs on top of the huur, for example for cleaning shared areas. Always read what is and is not included before you sign.

sections.title: Reparatie & problemen
sections.note: Use these to report a problem and arrange a repair.

items.en: The repair person is coming round.

sections.title: Opzeggen & een afspraak maken
sections.note: Phrases for giving notice and arranging a time.

items.en: I want to give notice on the home.

items.nl: Ik zeg het contract op per 1 juli.
items.en: I am giving notice on the contract as of 1 July.
Can you confirm this in writing?

items.nl: Wanneer komt u de meterstand opnemen?
items.en: When are you coming to read the meter?
Do I get the deposit back?

items.nl: Ik ben thuis na vijf uur.
items.en: I am at home after five o clock.

sections.title: Reading the meter
sections.body: When you move in or out, you note the meterstand (meter reading) for gas, water and electricity. This decides what you pay. Take a photo of the meters on the day you arrive and the day you leave, so there is no discussion later.

sections.q: De verwarming in uw huis is kapot. U belt de verhuurder. Wat zegt u?
sections.qEn: The heating in your home is broken. You call the landlord. What do you say?
options: De verwarming is kapot. Wanneer kunt u komen?
Ik wil graag een kilo kaas.
sections.answer: De verwarming is kapot. Wanneer kunt u komen?
sections.explanation: You first say what is wrong (De verwarming is kapot) and then ask when they can come to fix it. The other two answers belong to the cheese counter and to logging in online.
